# Death and the Undying · Book II, pp. 68–85
# Generated by the extractor — fix the extractor, not this file.
PAGE	68
P	Everyone who lives, dies.
P	When you succumb to injury or illness, or just reach the end of your allotted days, then the Last Door will swing open for you. You will see it. The Lady of Crows will beckon you through. And there on the other side, your soul will join those who have gone before: the honored ancestors, the countless multitudes of the quiet dead.
P	At least, that's how it's meant to go—the natural order of things. But not every soul passes through the Last Door when their time has come. Some linger, others are bound. Some are called back to this world.
P	Everyone who lives, dies. But not everyone dies the same.
H2	Themes
HR
P	Choose or roll 1, or 2 and combine.
P	1d12 theme
HR
P	1 Death personified: the Lady of Crows, the <b>Pale Hunter</b> (page 292), other gods/spirits of death
P	2 The Last Door/brushes with death/ the afterlife/things from beyond
P	3 Graves/funeral rites/grief/mourning
P	4 Death foretold: prophecies, omens, visions, harbingers
P	5 Good death: peaceful, dignified, bravely met, an end of suffering
PAGE	69
P	6 Ignoble death: traumatic, desperate, torturous, terrifying
P	7 Untimely death: sudden, surprising, things left unsaid or undone
P	8 Violent death: murder, assassination, execution, battle, suicide
P	9 Mass death: famine, plague, war, cataclysm, collapse
P	10 The fear of death: denial, bargaining, panic, cheating
P	11 The curse of undeath: respite denied, eternal hunger/pain/ loneliness/regret
P	12 Necromancy and death-magic, likely with aid from the <b>Things</b> <b>Below</b> (page 412)
H2	Hooks
HR
B	An abandoned house, out near the <b>Old</b> <b>Wall</b> (page 12), is said to be haunted.
B	A shade gets called up at the <b>Crossroads</b> (page 270) and refuses to go back.
B	A haunted grove near the <b>West Road</b> (page 270) is said to hide buried treasure.
B	A <b>necromancer</b> (page 84) comes to town, offering a chance to speak with the dearly departed.

H2	Questions
HR
Q	Have you seen the Last Door and the Lady of Crows? What do you recall?
Q	What do folks in Stonetop say awaits us, beyond the Last Door? What do they say in/among the __?
Q	What do you think awaits us? Why?
Q	Who among the dead do you miss most?
Q	What ghost story scared you the most as a child?
Q	When did you first see someone die?
Q	Who was the first person you murdered?
PAGE	70
H2	Death's Door
HR
P	When the PCs are dying and they make the <b>Death's Door</b> move (<i>Book I,</i> page 245), they see the Last Door and the Lady of Crows. The move prompts them to describe it, but feel free to ask questions.
Q	What does the Door look like? Big and grand, small and humble, or what?
Q	Is it flung open, or just ajar?
Q	What appears to lie beyond?
Q	Where does the Lady stand? What does she wear? What adorns her brow?
Q	What is she like? Imperious? Friendly? Sad? Smug? Inscrutable? Or what?
Q	Does she speak? What is her voice like? What does she say?
Q	What detail catches your attention, that you'd never have expected?
Q	How much of this will you remember?
P	As for the afterlife—the land beyond the Last Door—its true nature is a mystery.
P	But it is home to <b>dool spirits</b> (page 83), <b>gwyllgi</b> (page 84), and the <b>shades</b> (page 85) of the dead. Some of those shades, when called, are eager to stay in the land of the living. So for some, it would seem, the afterlife is not a pleasant place at all.
PAGE	71
H2	The Lady of Crows
HR
P	She has many titles. Carrion Queen and Black-Feather Woman. The Kindly One.
P	The Keeper of Secrets. She Who Dances on the Field of Battle. None know her true name, if she even has one. Most call her simply: the Lady of Crows.
P	Her nature and demeanor are for you and your table to decide, but ask/consider:
Q	What is her role? Psychopomp? Judge? Ruler of the afterlife? Or what?
Q	What does she want? What pleases her?
Q	Is she worshipped as a god? If so, what are her observances (page 184)?
Q	What is her origin said to be?
Q	What is her relationship to the <b>Pale</b> <b>Hunter</b> (page 292)?
Q	How do tales of her differ among __? What is notably the same?

H2	Dool trees
P	Dool trees often grow in or near haunted sites. A grove stands near the <b>Crossroads</b> (page 270), and lone dool trees are often found near <b>Barrow Builder</b> tombs (page 34).
P	They are thick and knobby and multi-stemmed. The bark is papery, the color of bleached bone. The <b>Pale</b> <b>Hunter</b> (page 292) shuns them, and they are often home to <b>dool spirits</b> (page 83) if nothing else.
P	The leaves of a dool tree are deep purple, almost black, shot through with pale white veins. Dried leaves can be steeped to make a bitter tea, which brings on a death-like sleep from which some folk never wake.

H3	A blackened splinter
P	<i>crude</i>, <i>magical</i>, <i>fireproof</i>
P	Undead who see it are drawn to it, or else deeply agitated by its presence. When you <b><i>touch the splinter to an undead entity,</i></b> they see the Last Door yawning open before them. Roll 4d6. If the total is greater than the entity's current HP, they are drawn through the Last Door and leave this world for good. Otherwise, they are transfixed for a few moments before the Door slams shut.
P	Regardless, the splinter vanishes.
HR
ICON	icons/treasure.svg
H3	A spindle of fine thread
P	<i>magical</i>
P	A length of fiber, maybe 50 feet long, spun by a ghost from all the hair that ever fell from her daughters' heads. The thread is light, and fine, and almost unbreakably strong, but it can be handled only by one who has seen the Last Door. Only the edge of a silver blade can cut it. It can be used to bind a ghost fast, if you're clever and can handle the thread yourself.
HR

H3	A pale wooden sword
P	◇, <i>close</i>, <i>crude</i>, <i>magical</i>
P	Carved from a dool tree with a silver knife, and polished with oils infused with moonlight. The grip is worn smooth but the "blade" is chipped and notched, unlikely to stand up to iron or bronze.
P	When you <b><i>wield the sword against a</i></b> <b><i>manifest undead spirit</i></b>, you can hurt it (deal damage normally). If you reduce it to
P	0 HP, the manifest form dissipates but the spirit can reform at its tether normally.
ICON	icons/treasure.svg
H3	A tattered standard
P	◇◇, <i>magical</i>
P	Threadbare, ancient, but remarkably well-preserved. Embroidered with a stylized aurochs whose horns encompass the sun. It fills you with hope and pride to look upon it, as well it should. For this was the standard of the Heol-Tarv, a heroic band who gave their lives in hopeless battle against the <b>Anan Gllo</b> (page 81), securing their people's escape.
P	When you <b><i>unfurl the tattered standard and</i></b> <b><i>hold it aloft for all to see</i></b>, you and your allies are immune to supernatural fear and unshaken by undead or otherwise unnatural foes.

H2	Ghosts
HR
P	Ghosts are the souls of the dead, those who linger in this world. They vary wildly in personality, motives, and capabilities, but all have the <i>undead</i> and <i>spirit</i> tags, and a move that reflects them manifesting a presence in the world. They are animated by more than biology (+4 HP) and lack vital organs (+3 HP, +1 armor).
P	Consider the context in which they are encountered. If not already established, pick or roll for their cause of death (page 73). Then pick or roll for what they need to move on, their manifestation, and 1-6 abilities and/or weaknesses. Establish their <b>tether</b> (page 77). Let all these elements inform their story and their stat block.
P	1d12 what they need
HR
P	1-2 Kindness/patience/persuasion, a guide to the Last Door
P	3-4 Justice (or vengeance) served
P	5-6 A proper burial
P	7 A reunion with a loved one
P	8 The truth, unearthed/acknowledged
P	9 A task completed; an oath fulfilled
P	10-11 Their tether, destroyed or unmade
P	12 To be put down, like a rabid dog
P	1d12 manifestation
HR
P	1 Just a whisper/wind/mote of light*
P	2-3 A form of shadow/cold/mist/etc*
P	4-6 A spectral form, ethereal and eerie, but much as they looked in life*
P	7-9 A spectral form, horrible, clearly dead*
P	10 A body made of soil/straw/rags/etc.
P	11 A solid body, horrific and terrifying
P	12 A solid body, seemingly alive but for a few telltale signs
P	* Harmed only by silver or salt, or some other thematically appropriate substances
P	1d12 ability
HR
P	1-2 Causes eerie, unnatural phenomena
P	3 Feels (feeds on?) emotions/vitality/ sensations of the living
P	4 Can possess certain hosts/vessels
P	5 Unearthly moan/wail/shriek
P	6 Inflicts its pain/feelings on others
P	7-8 Telekinesis (roll 1d6 for scope)
P	9 Nasty/vicious/ghostly attack
P	10 Mind games/phantasms/ compulsions
P	11-12 Can manifest in multiple forms
P	1d12 weakness
HR
P	1 Afraid of some mundane thing
P	2 Inarticulate, or unable to speak
P	3 Obsessive/predictable behavior
P	4 Easily frustrated/angered/enraged
P	5 Can't form new memories
P	6 Driven off by singing/prayer/etc.
P	7-12 Shuns/powerless in daylight
PAGE	77
H3	Tethers
P	Ghosts are bound to an object or place.
P	Pick or roll for the tether itself, and how tightly bound the ghost is.
P	1d12 tether
HR
P	1-4 Their corpse/remains/bones/hair
P	5-6 The place where they died
P	7 (Part of) their grave/pyre/altar/etc.
P	8 The weapon that killed them
P	9 An item they once cherished
P	10 A prominent place from their life
P	11-12 The focus/source of whatever magic binds them
P	1d12 how tightly bound
HR
P	1-2 Can't leave its immediate presence
P	3-6 Must stay on the premises/site
P	7-10 Can roam a few miles; returns daily
P	11-12 Can wander far and wide, but must return periodically If a ghost's manifest form is reduced to
P	0 HP, they dissipate and return to their tether. They usually won't manifest before the next sunset; if they do, their max HP are halved.
P	If a tether is destroyed, then the ghost might… (pick 1)
E	fade away, utterly destroyed;
E	pass through the Last Door (now, or after some final act);
E	devolve into a <b>wraith</b> (page 79);
E	possess a corpse, as a <b>pyped</b> (page 82); or
E	cling to their current host/form, but fade utterly if it is destroyed.
P	Decide based on the ghost's history, power, and relationship to their tether.

H3	The Gwraig Wen
P	<i>Solitary</i>, <i>spirit</i>, <i>undead</i>, <i>forlorn</i>
P	<b>HP</b> 19; <b>Armor</b> 1 (lacks organs)
P	<b>Damage</b> bare hands d6 w/disadvantage (<i>hand</i>)
P	<b>Special qualities</b> bound to within a few miles of her bones; can't form new memories; leaves no footprints <b>Instinct</b> to drag others into her search
P	• Manifest in moonlight as a pale, bedraggled woman
P	• Ask for help, insist on it
P	• Grow ever more agitated, flickering and vibrating as she does
P	• Vent her rage with a deafening wail, d10 damage (<i>near</i>, <i>area</i>, <i>loud</i>, <i>reload</i>, ignores armor)
P	• Vanish when no one's looking
P	Those who ply the <b>Great Wood</b> (page 200) tell an old tale of a bride, newly married to a handsome trapper. He failed to come home one night, and she unwisely entered the forest to find him, falling into a deep pond and drowning. Ever since, her ghost has roamed the woods on moonlit nights: wet and shivering, desperate and pleading, certain that her husband is still out there.

H3	The Ghostly Legion
P	<i>Horde</i>, <i>spirit</i>, <i>undead</i>, <i>organized,</i> <i>terrifying</i>, <i>hoarder</i>, <i>violent</i>
P	<b>HP</b> 10; <b>Armor</b> 1 (lacks organs)
P	<b>Damage</b> ghostly short sword or spear d6 w/advantage (<i>hand</i>, <i>close</i>)
P	<b>Special qualities</b> roams far and wide, but tethered to the cave; shuns daylight; can only touch the world through violence; upsetting to/afraid of dogs
P	<b>Instinct</b> to lift their curse
P	• Manifest a spectral form (harmed only by silver, salt, or a loyal dog)
P	• Ogle a mortal as they eat or drink
P	• Threaten violence, carry through
P	• Force a mortal to carry their treasure
P	They were a band of southern mercenaries, come north in search of treasure. They heard tell of a <b>hdour</b> (page 234) and his hoard, trapped him in his cave, and slew him. Then they divvied up the loot and left.
P	Only later did they learn why the Hillfolk fear to kill a hdour. For he had cursed them all. Cursed their souls to linger after death, doomed to endless hunger and endless thirst.
P	Doomed to fear the sun, to be hounded like the dogs they were. Cursed, indeed, until every piece of the far-flung loot they stole is returned to the hdour's cave.

H3	Specter
P	<i>Solitary</i>, <i>spirit</i>, <i>undead</i>, <i>stealthy</i>, <i>terrifying</i>, <i>cruel</i>
P	<b>HP</b> 23; <b>Armor</b> 1 (lacks vitals)
P	<b>Damage</b> telekinesis d10+2 (<i>hand</i>, <i>close</i>,
P	<i>near</i>, <i>grabby</i>, <i>forceful</i>)
P	<b>Special qualities</b> bound to its tether; one or more weaknesses (page 76)
P	<b>Instinct</b> to torment the living
P	• Create eerie environmental effects (bleeding walls, green flames, etc.)
P	• Manifest a form of flitting shadow (harmed only by silver or salt)
P	• Manifest a nightmarish physical form
P	• Speak through an unconscious or catatonic victim
P	A specter is a soul consumed by hatred and envy, cruelty and rage. Maybe they were a sadistic murderer in life, or a victim whose death was so traumatic that they lash out at any living thing. Maybe they were a pining ghost whose loved ones rejected them, or a fettered soul long- and cruelly-bound, now set free. Regardless: they are now a thing of spite and vengeance, wanting only to punish those with the temerity to live.

H3	Wraith
P	<i>Solitary</i>, <i>spirit</i>, <i>undead</i>, <i>stealthy</i>, <i>terrifying</i>
P	<b>HP</b> 19; <b>Armor</b> 1 (lacks organs)
P	<b>Damage</b> life drain d10 (<i>hand</i>, ignores armor)
P	<b>Special qualities</b> bound to its tether (usually), powerless in daylight <b>Instinct</b> to feast upon living souls
P	• Manifest a form of shadow and cold (harmed only by silver and salt)
P	• Hurl itself at the living
P	• Suck vitality from its prey
P	Wraiths are cursed with endless hunger.
P	They are damaged souls, wounded by dark magic, another wraith, or the dehumanizing effects of starvation or addiction. They are little more than beasts, driven by the emptiness within, with only the vaguest sense of who they once were.
P	Other ghosts might become wraiths when their tethers are destroyed. If they linger in the world, they find themselves filled with gnawing need, and must sustain themselves on the living. These unbound wraiths are weaker, but often form packs with others of their kind (<i>group</i>, <i>vicious</i> instead of <i>stealthy</i>,
P	13 HP each, d8 damage, afraid of firelight).
P	When <b><i>a wraith reduces you to 0 HP and</i></b> <b><i>you survive</i></b>, your soul is wounded. Reduce your max HP by 4. Until your soul is healed, your instinct becomes "Hunger: to fill the emptiness inside you with excess," and should you roll a 6- on Death's Door, you die and become a wraith (a monster in the GM's control).

H2	Revenants
HR
P	Revenants are the living dead, corpses animated by a soul, a demon, or foul magic.
P	They vary wildly in personality, motives, and capabilities. They are <i>undead</i>, animated by more than biology (+4 HP).
P	Consider the context in which a revenant is encountered. If not yet established, pick or roll for their cause of death (page 73). Then pick or roll for what they were brought back by, their visage, and 1-6 abilities and/or weaknesses. Let all these elements inform their story and their stat block.
P	1d12 brought back by
HR
P	1-3 A thirst for vengeance
P	4 A longing that transcends death
P	5 Stubbornness/habit/will
P	6 Guilt, like heavy chains
P	7-8 An oath/vow, stronger than iron
P	9 A curse, well-deserved or not
P	10 Their own designs, some dark ritual/deal/preparation
P	11-12 The will or working of another (and maybe roll 1d10 for why/how)
P	1d12 visage
HR
P	1-2 Naught but bone, a grinning skull
P	3-5 Tattered, rotting, horrible
P	6-8 Dried out, gaunt, clearly dead; but can pass for living at a distance
P	9-10 Seemingly alive, but clearly dead and horrible in sun/moonlight
P	11-12 Seemingly alive, except for a few telltale signs
P	1d12 ability
HR
P	1 Uncanny speed/grace/prowess
P	2 Unholy strength (<i>forceful</i>, +2 damage)
P	3-4 Unnatural resilience (+4 HP, +4 armor except vs. silver or fire)
P	5-6 Can regenerate/reform/rise again
P	7 Limbs that can keep acting and reattach even if severed
P	8 Minions (bugs, its own severed hand or floating eye, a crow, etc.)
P	9 Mesmerizing/terrifying gaze
P	10 Aura of cold/heat/smoke/rot/etc.
P	11 Magic, related to how they died
P	12 Shapeshifting (mist/beasts/etc.)
P	1d12 weakness
HR

P	2 Fire (fears it/takes +1d4 damage/etc.)
P	3 Bound to a <b>tether</b> (page 77)
P	4 Hungers for blood/flesh/life/fear/etc.

P	6 Compulsively counts/cleans/sorts/etc.
P	7 Easily frustrated/confused/provoked

H3	Anan Gllo
P	<i>Horde</i>, <i>undead</i>, <i>corrupted</i>, <i>tireless</i>, <i>fearless</i>, <i>terrifying</i>
P	<b>HP</b> 11; <b>Armor</b> 5 (resilience, armor), 1 vs.
P	bronze or fire <b>Damage</b> weapon d6 (tags by weapon) or crushing grip d4 (<i>hand</i>, <i>grabby</i>)
P	<b>Special qualities</b> weaken over time (see below)
P	<b>Instinct</b> to follow orders
P	• Advance implacably
P	• Unnerve foes with their silence, their empty eyes
P	• Fight on despite crippling injury
P	The <b>Hillfolk</b> (page 228) speak of dark times, when the <b>Things Below</b> (page 412) gave a gift to a petty chief. Depending on who tells the tale, it was a patch of loose soil or a deep pool of water, the hollow of a dool tree or a great cauldron of rusted iron.
P	Regardless: a corpse placed within this vessel would rise as one of the Anan Gllo, the Empty Dead. The chief raised an undead army, and set out to make themselves king.
P	<b>Something interesting:</b> The chief 's power was broken when a hero entered the vessel while still alive, giving their life to destroy it. A number of Anan Gllo linger, though, inert and waiting.
P	<b>Something useful:</b> An Anan Gllo regains all its HP when it either drinks fresh blood or re-enters the vessel; it cannot otherwise regain HP. And every dawn, an Anan Gllo loses 1 HP. At 0 HP, it becomes inert until its HP are restored.
ICON	icons/undead.svg
H3	Dialeddwr
P	<i>Solitary</i>, <i>undead</i>, <i>terrifying</i>, <i>implacable</i>
P	<b>HP</b> 20; <b>Armor</b> 4 (resilience), 0 vs. silver or fire <b>Damage</b> choking grip or powerful blows d8+2 w/advantage (<i>hand</i>, <i>grabby</i>, <i>forceful</i>)
P	<b>Special qualities</b> cannot open doors, eat, or drink
P	<b>Instinct</b> to avenge
P	• Pass for alive, except in sunlight
P	• Unerringly track a target
P	• Lock eyes with someone, show them the meaning of fear
P	• Bask in moonlight to regenerate even terrible wounds
P	Sometimes, when a great wrong is done, when a good person is cruelly slain, when the killers go unpunished… well, sometimes they come back. Called back by a prayer or perhaps a spell. Or sent back by their fellow victims. Or guided back by one of the Lady's own crows. They dig themselves free of their graves, reborn and whole. And vengeance shall be theirs.

H3	Pyped
P	<i>Solitary</i>, <i>undead</i>, <i>terrifying</i>, <i>craven</i>
P	<b>HP</b> 16; <b>Armor</b> 1 (speed)
P	<b>Damage</b> bone-snapping grip d8+2 (<i>hand</i>,
P	<i>grabby</i>, <i>forceful</i>)
P	<b>Special qualities</b> burned by silver (+1d4 damage); harmed by salt (1d8 damage, <i>hand</i>, <i>close</i>); foul stench; sustained by bone marrow
P	<b>Instinct</b> to avoid the Last Door
P	• Move with a surprising, jerky speed
P	• Jumble up its memories with those of its host & those whose bones it's eaten
P	• Possess a new corpse, if it can/must
P	When an untethered <b>ghost</b> (page 76) or a <b>shade</b> (page 85) possesses an empty corpse, it becomes a pyped. They are wretched things, all rotting flesh and lurching movements, hungering for sweet marrow, scavenging on carrion and graves. But hunger can make them bold. Bold enough to hunt the weak and sick at the edge of a village, or a lone traveler caught unawares.
P	Pypeds rise only from corpses that are relatively intact, and which have not undergone proper funeral rites. If a pyped is destroyed, the spirit within will seek a new, viable corpse. A shade must find one before the sun banishes it. An untethered ghost must find one before its memories fade and it becomes a <b>wraith</b> (page 79).
ICON	icons/undead.svg
H3	Ulliam Unlucky
P	<i>Solitary</i>, <i>undead</i>, <i>stealthy</i>, <i>terrifying</i>, <i>loyal</i>
P	<b>HP</b> 16; <b>Armor</b> 0 <b>Damage</b> whatever's at hand d8 w/disadvantage (tags vary)
P	<b>Special qualities</b> burned/blinded by daylight; chill aura <b>Instinct</b> to pine for his family
P	• Keep out of sight, or try to
P	• Get frustrated, agitated, angry
P	• Lose his temper and drain heat from someone, d10 damage w/advantage (<i>hand</i>, <i>close</i>, <i>reach</i>, ignores armor)
P	Ulliam Unlucky dragged his family from <b>Marshedge</b> (page 274) up to <b>Gordin's</b> <b>Delve</b> (page 190), in search of a better life. But things never did work out. Last time he went out prospecting, he got lost.
P	Then the blizzard rolled in. And that's how Ulliam died.
P	But say what you will about Ulliam, he loved his wife and kids. Still does. Dragged his frozen self home to see 'em again. He knows they can't see him like this, but he can't keep himself from lurking. And when some lech comes sniffing around his wife, or some fool notices him and makes a fuss… well, there's only so much a man can take. And that little spark of warmth he draws out of them? Well, he's starting to acquire a taste.

ICON	icons/spirit.svg
H3	Dool spirit
P	<i>Group</i>, <i>spirit</i>, <i>terrifying</i>, <i>stealthy</i>, <i>devious</i>
P	<b>HP</b> 13; <b>Armor</b> 1 (lacks organs)
P	<b>Damage</b> feast on fears d6 w/disadvantage (<i>hand</i>, <i>close</i>, ignores armor)
P	<b>Special qualities</b> powerless in bright light; bound to its tree or a victim's bones <b>Instinct</b> to taste sweet, delicious fears
P	• Sense a victim's doubt and worries
P	• Shape sound and shadow to unnerve and frighten
P	• Manifest as its victim's fears (harmed only by one who masters their fear)
P	• Bind itself to a victim's bones
P	Dool spirits hail from beyond the Last Door. They are not undead, for they never lived, but are native to the afterlife. They sometimes slip into this world, haunting the <b>dool trees</b> (page 73) from which they get their name.
P	When a dool spirit takes a liking to a victim's fears, it leaves its tree and binds itself to that victim's very bones. It proceeds to haunt them, and only them, driving them mad with fear. The spirit remains bound to that victim's bones even in death, until a new dool tree sprouts where those bones are buried, and the spirit can haunt the living once more.

H3	Gwyllgi
P	<i>Solitary</i>, <i>spirit</i>, <i>cautious</i>, <i>stealthy</i>, <i>terrifying</i>
P	<b>HP</b> 16; <b>Armor</b> 4 (resilience, 0 vs. silver)
P	<b>Damage</b> claws d8 (<i>close</i>) or bite d8+2
P	(<i>hand</i>, <i>grabby</i>, <i>forceful</i>)
P	<b>Special qualities</b> hates daylight, must be manifest to feed <b>Instinct</b> to feed on fear and despair
P	• Manifest as a black wolf with blazing red eyes
P	• Appear to someone out alone at night and lay a <b>death curse</b> on them (see below)
P	• Breathe forth a baleful cloud, d6 damage (<i>reach</i>, <i>area</i>, ignores armor)
P	A gwyllgi is a harbinger of death, a being from beyond. A necromancer might call one forth to send against their foes. Or, one might slip through the Last Door when dark magic or the death of many cause it to swing wide open.

ICON	icons/danger.svg
H3	Death curse
P	Threat (<i>affliction</i>)
P	<b>Instinct</b> to crank up tension and dread
P	• Cause an accident or coincidence
P	• Drive them to anxiety, desperation
P	• Push them towards a bad decision
P	• Get them, in the end
P	When <b><i>a gwyllgi curses a victim</i></b>, they know they will die before the next full moon.
P	<b>Something interesting:</b> A gwyllgi can curse only one victim at a time, and it manifests each night to feed on its victim's emotions.
P	<b>Something useful:</b> You can lift the curse by destroying the gwyllgi's form, banishing it back through the Last Door.
ICON	icons/person.svg
H3	Necromancer
P	<i>Solitary</i>, <i>cautious</i>, <i>cunning</i>, <i>magical</i>, <i>death-wise</i>
P	<b>HP</b> 12; <b>Armor</b> 0 (or by worn armor)
P	<b>Damage</b> silver-alloy knife d8 (<i>hand</i>)
P	<b>Special qualities</b> can sense active spirits
P	<b>Instinct</b> to hoard secrets/knowledge
P	• Call up, speak with, bind, or lose control of an undead entity
P	• Reveal or act on knowledge they should not possess
P	• Send the undead against a foe
P	• Cast a death-related spell (<i>reload</i>)
P	'Tis an odd sort, who would have truck with spirits of the dead. But some are born with the Sight, and a morbid curiosity. If they can avoid getting themselves killed by hungry ghosts or outraged locals…
P	well, the dead have all manner of secrets to teach.
P	Necromancers often find themselves consorting with entities even darker than the dead, and are prone to <b>corruption</b> (page 430) by the Things Below. They are likely to possess one or more <b>arcana</b> (page 508), which they do not hesitate to use. And they are often attended by one or more bound entities.

ICON	icons/undead.svg
H3	Shade
P	<i>Solitary</i>, <i>spirit</i>, <i>undead</i>, <i>cautious</i>
P	<b>HP</b> 19; <b>Armor</b> 1 (lacks organs)
P	<b>Damage</b> none
P	<b>Special qualities</b> banished by daylight <b>Instinct</b> (pick 1 or roll 1d6) 1: to refuse to go back, 2: to fulfill its longings, 3-4: to bemoan its fate, 5-6: to return to its rest
P	• Manifest as a whisper and a dim image, unable to affect the physical world
P	• Share what it knew in life
P	• Reveal a secret learned in death
P	• "Ride" a willing/prepared host
P	• Possess an intact and uninterred corpse, creating a <b>pyped</b> (page 82)
P	Shades are the souls of the quiet dead, called back through the Last Door. Or perhaps they are merely echoes of a dead person's personality, given shape by magic.
P	Either way, they might be called up at the <b>Crossroads</b> (page 270), via an arcanum like <b>a strange skull and antlers</b> (page 520), or by some other form of necromancy.
P	A shade can ride a living, willing host, or one who has been properly prepared (with arcane markings, by bearing an appropriate object, via a potion, etc.). It can withstand daylight while doing so, but only with great effort. It experiences what its host experiences, and can communicate with its host via only impulse and desire.
P	When <b><i>a shade rides you and compels you to</i></b> <b><i>act against your will,</i></b> mark XP if you do as it wants. If you resist, you are Defying Danger.
ICON	icons/spirit.svg
H3	Tomb-bog spirit
P	<i>Solitary</i>, <i>spirit</i>, <i>terrifying</i>, <i>implacable</i>
P	<b>HP</b> 19; <b>Armor</b> 1 (lacks organs)
P	<b>Damage</b> smothering grip d10+2 (<i>hand</i>,
P	<i>forceful</i>, <i>grabby</i>)
P	<b>Special qualities</b> harms only those whose life is forfeit <b>Instinct</b> to consume the dying breaths of the condemned
P	• Track down one whose life is forfeit
P	• Wait until they are alone
P	• Shape a hulking form from peat, soil, and mud (takes half damage from stabbing, slashing, or fire)
P	• Whisper its victim's crimes, freezing them with fear
P	In <b>Ferrier's Fen</b> (page 116), not far from <b>Marshedge</b> (page 274), there lies a peat mound where the town buries criminals alive. Over the years, the place has given birth to a spirit of death and punishment.
P	The spirit is young and eager, and can be set to work upon criminals; see the <b>grim</b> <b>peat mound</b> (page 511) minor arcanum for details.
